ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Determine the AC voltage at point "B" in the circuit diagram after the AC signal voltage passes through the voltage divider biasing network, given a 9 kHz sinusoidal voltage of 0.5 volts (peak) at point "A". The AC voltage at point "B" is ______ VAC.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, point A is located at the node after the three 50 kΩ input resistors on the left converge; a 47 µF capacitor is connected in series from A to point B. Point B is also connected to a voltage-divider bias network composed of 81 kΩ pulled up to VCC = +12 VDC and 10 kΩ pulled down to ground, and is connected to the transistor base through a 33 kΩ resistor. The figure also shows collector 4.7 kΩ, output coupling capacitor 220 µF, emitter 1 kΩ, and bypass capacitor 100 µF. Reasoning: The problem gives that at point A there is a 9 kHz, 0.5 V peak sinusoidal AC signal. When making the AC equivalent, VCC is regarded as ground for AC, so the 81 kΩ and 10 kΩ voltage-divider resistors at point B form a high-impedance load to AC ground. The reactance of the 47 µF capacitor at 9 kHz is Xc = 1/(2π·9000·47 µF) ≈ 0.38 Ω, far smaller than the kΩ-level bias resistor load. Therefore this coupling capacitor produces almost no AC attenuation between A and B, and the AC voltage at point B is approximately equal to the AC voltage at point A.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: identify node A feeding node B through the 47 µF capacitor, with B tied to the 81 kΩ and 10 kΩ voltage-divider bias resistors. From the text, take the input at A as a 9 kHz sine wave of 0.5 V peak. Convert the circuit to its AC equivalent: VCC is AC ground and the bias resistors become a high-resistance load at B. Compute or estimate the capacitor reactance at 9 kHz: Xc = 1/(2π·9000·47 µF), which is far below the kΩ bias resistances. Therefore the 47 µF capacitor produces essentially no attenuation between A and B, so the AC voltage at B equals the AC voltage at A: 0.5 VAC.

planner_metadata.image_role: Read from the diagram that point A is on the left of a 47 µF coupling capacitor, point B is on the right of that capacitor, and B is connected to an 81 kΩ/10 kΩ voltage-divider bias network plus the transistor base path. planner_metadata.text_role: Read the given signal frequency, 9 kHz, and the input amplitude at point A, 0.5 V peak, from the question statement.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: For AC small-signal analysis, DC supply rails are AC ground.
